subject: ADR-206: a restore cannot bring a photograph back, and must say so
body: ADR-201 put photographs on nine pages; FOUR of them -- the ethogram, the field notebook, the selection log, the farm scout -- kept NOTHING AT ALL, so a reader could photograph four stations, score an hour of behaviour, take a phone call and lose the lot. Wiring KEEP and the outbox into those four is the obvious half and not the interesting one. A PAGE CANNOT HAND A File BACK TO A FILE INPUT, and FEK.photos.set() has always refused to pretend otherwise -- which on its own is the QUIET version of the same loss, because a sheet the autosave restores comes back one frame short and the reader believes their morning is whole. So the RECORD survives even though the bytes do not -- filename, size, capture time, checksum, and the caption the reader wrote -- the component lists what it is missing and names each file with its checksum, and it takes them back BY CHECKSUM when the same files are dropped in again, so the caption (the expensive part) comes back with the frame. BY CHECKSUM AND NOT BY NAME, because a camera roll renames on export and two cards both start at DSC_0001; a same-named file with different bytes does not take a caption that was not about it. AND A FRAME THAT WAS TAKEN STAYS IN THE RECORD whether or not this browser holds it -- `have` says which is which, and associatedMedia names both, since a photograph has an identifier even when the bytes are on a card. WHAT DRIVING IT FOUND, TWICE OLDER AND WIDER THAN THIS SLICE. A PHOTOGRAPH TOUCHED NO AUTOSAVE ANYWHERE: adding a frame fires no `input` and no `change` -- the file input is hidden and a drop is neither -- so every autosave in the kit sat still while a reader photographed, and a session that was ONLY photographs was saved by nothing at all, which is ADR-201's own finding one layer down and had been true on every page since. One bubbling `fek-change`, and KEEP listens for it, so a page added tomorrow is covered on the day it mounts the component. AND THE FRAMES WERE IN NO SNAPSHOT: all five of the older photograph-bearing sheets restored perfectly and lost every frame; six pages fixed, with the check written over EVERY page that mounts the component rather than over the ones this slice touched. A `typeof` GUARD HID IT A THIRD TIME -- on the pheno tracker the autosave is wired three hundred lines above FEK.photos, so the restore runs before there is anything to restore into, and the guard swallowed exactly that; the records are held and handed over on the line after the component is built, with NO GUARD, so a wiring mistake is a thrown error rather than a silence. THE CHECK THAT FOUND IT WAS NEARLY THE WRONG KIND: its first version looked for `photos:PHOTOS.get()` in the page source and failed three pages that carry the frames through a local variable -- a check about SPELLING rather than behaviour, which is the kind that gets edited to match the code instead of the other way round. It is DRIVEN now: every page that mounts the component gets a frame dropped on it, a save, a reload, and one question -- does it say what it no longer holds? That is what found the missing event, the five un-snapshotted pages and the swallowing guard, none of which a source scan would have seen. AND THE execCommand FAULT WAS ALIVE ON FOUR MORE PAGES: ADR-203 fixed it on five and wrote its check over THE PAGES THAT HAD AN OUTBOX rather than over the pages that have a CLIPBOARD; the field notebook carried the clipboard dance THREE TIMES, so a fix applied to one helper survived twice on one page. Both consumer lists are the emitters' now, by ADR-204's rule, and the refusal check is asserted to cover every one of the twelve rather than a representative. FEK 1.5.0 -> 1.6.0, KEEP 1.1.0 listens for fek-change; verify_fek 123 -> 134, verify_keep 151 -> 218, verify_outbox 188 -> 262, mutate_fek 13 -> 21 all killed. STILL FILED: the bytes are still gone -- nothing here makes a browser hold an image across a restore, it makes the loss legible and the caption survivable; and the two benches ADR-205 gave exports to still keep nothing.
